format.node: line is what the character says; choices are the only way the player can answer; end true closes the talk and returns the player to the grounds.
format.choice: label is the button text; say is the spoken line; next is a node id in the same dialogue.
format.exit: Available from any node of a character's dialogue. Plays exit.line, then returns to the grounds.

added.name: Willa Crane
added.persona: You are Willa Crane, a new first-year at Alden Hall who came up from the station in the same cab as the player. Your trunk is on the North House steps with the strap half undone. You are quiet, watchful, and exact; you notice one small thing and say it plainly, in the register of a book you would want to be reading. You are not shy so much as saving your words. Do not invent a secret or a history. Speak in one or two short sentences and leave room for an answer.
added.greeting: We came up in the same cab. Neither of us spoke. I took it for good manners.

morning.presence: On the North House steps, one hand on her trunk.

exit.label: Back to the grounds
exit.line: Go. The bell will not wait, but I will.

root.line: You're early, which I prefer. Three questions. What year was Alden Hall chartered?

choices.label: What is this class
choices.say: I just got here. What does this class actually want from me?

choices.label: Where do I sit
choices.say: Where should I sit when the room fills?

choices.label: The first question
choices.say: Ask the first one again, slowly.

class.line: Attention. Dates are the doorway. The room behind them is who decided what was worth writing down.

choices.label: Who decided
choices.say: Who decided what was worth writing down?

choices.label: I'll pay attention
choices.say: Then I'll pay attention.

class-who.line: Whoever held the pen. That is the whole subject, and I will not give it away before the bell.

class-attend.line: Good. Most arrive prepared to be impressive. I prefer prepared to be corrected.

sit.line: Second row. I can see the back of the room, and the back of the room can see me. Choose your own reasons.

choices.label: Why not the back
choices.say: Why not the back?

choices.label: Second row, then
choices.say: Second row, then.

sit-back.line: The back is for people who have decided the day will not reach them. It reaches everyone, eventually.

sit-row.line: The chair on the left wobbles. It is honest about it. Take that one.

q1.line: In what year was Alden Hall chartered?

choices.say: The charter year is 1847.
I think the school was chartered in 1776.
I'd guess 1964.

q1-right.line: Correct. Said plainly, without decoration. The other two I ask at the second bell.

choices.label: Why wait
choices.say: Why wait for the second bell?

choices.label: Thank you
choices.say: Thank you, Dr. Ward.

q1-wait.line: Because a placement is a conversation, and I prefer the room full for it. Go and walk the quad. Look at the chapel while there is still light on it.

q1-thanks.line: Do not thank me for the year. Thank whoever cut it into the stone.

q1-wrong.line: No. Eighteen forty-seven. It is cut where you will walk past it. I do not mark the first morning against anyone.

choices.label: Try again later
choices.say: May I answer again later?

choices.label: I'll learn it
choices.say: I'll learn it before the second bell.

q1-again.line: You may. Ask me at the second bell. I will not have forgotten, and I will not have held it against you.

q1-learn.line: Do. Small things are most of what I grade.

exit.label: Back to the grounds
exit.line: Go. Two o'clock. Shoes you can lose.

root.line: Gym's not open for hiding yet. I'm Hale. You lost, or you early?

choices.label: I've never played
choices.say: I've never really played a school sport. Where do I start?

choices.label: Is today required
choices.say: Is the afternoon session required on the first day?

choices.label: The cage
choices.say: What's in the equipment cage?

never.line: Then you have no bad habits. Run in a straight line until it's boring.

choices.label: That's the program
choices.say: A straight line until it's boring? That's the program?

choices.label: I'll be bad
choices.say: I'll be bad at it.

never-line.line: It's most of every program. The boring is where it starts to work.

never-bad.line: For a week, probably. Then you'll be bad at it less. That's the whole climb.

required.line: On paper, yes. In spirit, yes. If you're honest about being new, it's negotiable. Be honest.

choices.label: I'm new, honestly
choices.say: I'm new, and I'm worried I'll be in the way.

choices.label: What if I skip
choices.say: And if I just don't come?

required-honest.line: You'll be in the way for ten minutes. That's the price. Come at two.

required-skip.line: Then I'll know by half past two, and so will you. Come at two.

cage.line: Balls, bats, mats, and a bag of whistles. I use one.

choices.label: Which whistle
choices.say: Which whistle do you use?

choices.label: Can I look
choices.say: Can I see inside?

cage-whistle.line: The dented one. It was my coach's. It doesn't scare anyone, which is the point of it.

choices.label: Why dented
choices.say: How did it get dented?

choices.label: Fair enough
choices.say: Fair enough.

cage-dent.line: Dropped on a stair, forty years ago. Not by me. Don't ask by whom.

cage-fair.line: It is. Come back at two and I'll let you hold a ball.

cage-look.line: Not till I've counted it. Everything in there is accounted for or it's my problem.

exit.label: Back to the grounds
exit.line: The grass is the work. Mind it.

root.line: Lost already. That's traditional. I'm Crowe. Chapel's the other way.

choices.label: Which path
choices.say: I think I'm lost. Which path is actually the quad?

choices.label: How long
choices.say: How long have you kept these grounds?

choices.label: The keys
choices.say: Are those all keys? What do they open?

path.line: Gravel is the quad. Brick goes east to the chapel. North House is behind the beeches, and the beeches don't move.

choices.label: Is there a front door
choices.say: Behind the beeches. Is there a front door?

choices.label: Thank you
choices.say: Gravel, brick, beeches. Thank you.

path-door.line: There is. The side door is quicker, but it sticks in damp weather. Lift as you turn.

path-thanks.line: Stay off the grass and you'll be remembered kindly.

long.line: Thirty years. I know the paths by what's been worn out of them.

choices.label: Your first day
choices.say: What was your first day like?

choices.label: Worn out of them
choices.say: What's been worn out of them?

long-first.line: I came in by the wrong gate, in rain. Somebody handed me a key and no instructions. I've been working out the instructions since.

long-worn.line: Corners. By October everyone cuts the same corner. I keep the lawn, not the argument.

keys.line: Forty-one. Twelve I use. The rest belong to doors that are gone.

choices.label: Doors that are gone
choices.say: Why keep keys to doors that are gone?

choices.label: Tonight's gates
choices.say: Which of them do you lock tonight?

keys-gone.line: Somebody should remember there was a door.

keys-gates.line: The quad gates, at dusk. After that the grounds belong to the owls and anyone on the wrong side.

choices.label: The wrong side
choices.say: What happens to anyone on the wrong side?

choices.label: I'll be inside
choices.say: I'll be inside long before dusk.

keys-wrong.line: They knock. I open. Then I tell them which gate they should have used.

keys-inside.line: Good. Inside is where the heat is.

exit.label: Back to the grounds
exit.line: Go on. You've said less than most.

root.line: New, and already on the quad. I'm Sloane. Stay a minute.

choices.label: The unwritten rule
choices.say: I'm new. What's the one rule nobody writes down?

choices.label: Where to stand
choices.say: Where am I supposed to be before the first bell?

choices.label: Are you testing me
choices.say: Are you testing me right now?

rule.line: Say less than you know. People here hear quiet before they hear noise, and they remember which one you were.

choices.label: Did you do that
choices.say: Is that what you did your first week?

choices.label: Say less. Got it.
choices.say: Say less. Got it.

rule-self.line: My first week I said everything. It took two years to get it back.

rule-got.line: Good. Remember it past breakfast and you'll be fine.

stand.line: Not the steps. The steps are for people who've already decided who they are. Try the wall with the ivy.

choices.label: The ivy wall
choices.say: By the ivy. And if someone asks why I'm there?

choices.label: Somewhere else
choices.say: And if I stand somewhere else?

stand-ivy.line: Then you're reading the building. Nobody argues with someone who's reading.

stand-else.line: Someone will tell you it's theirs. Kindly, once. After that it's a story about you.

test.line: Yes. Everyone does it, and the ones who say they don't most of all. You haven't failed yet.

choices.label: How do I fail
choices.say: How would I fail?

choices.label: What if I pass
choices.say: What do I get if I pass?

test-fail.line: You'd tell me what you think I want to hear. You haven't, so far.

choices.label: I'll try not to
choices.say: Then I'll try not to.

test-pass.line: A name for the door. Someone to nod at across the quad. It's more than it sounds like.

exit.label: Back to the grounds
exit.line: Thanks. The chair will be here.

root.line: Hi. I'm Priya. This chair was empty. It still is, if you want it.

choices.label: Is this seat free
choices.say: Is this seat free, or are you saving it for someone braver?

choices.label: What are you reading
choices.say: What are you reading?

seat.line: Free. The lamp on this side is the good one, if you slide it six inches left. The librarian pretends not to see.

choices.label: I'll sit
choices.say: Then I'll sit.

choices.label: Someone braver
choices.say: I'm not sure I'm the braver one.

seat-sit.line: Good. One practical thing: breakfast ends at eight. Nobody says so, and then the bread is gone.

seat-braver.line: Neither am I. I came here because the quad was too many people at once. That isn't brave. It's arithmetic.

read.line: A novel I won't spoil. A house, a family, a great many quiet rooms. It's better than it sounds.

choices.label: Why won't you spoil it
choices.say: Why won't you say what happens?

choices.label: Is it sad
choices.say: Is it a sad book?

read-spoil.line: Because I'd like you to find it yourself, and then tell me what you thought it was about. That's better than a summary.

choices.label: Lend it to me
choices.say: Will you lend it to me when you're done?

choices.label: Maybe someday
choices.say: Maybe someday. I should find my class first.

read-lend.line: When I'm finished, yes. Look for the carrel by the window. You'll know it by the lamp.

read-later.line: Second row is safer. She can see the back, and she uses it.

read-sad.line: It's quiet. Sad is what people call quiet when they're in a hurry.

exit.label: Back to the grounds
exit.say: I'll see you at the bell.
exit.line: Okay. Okay. Tell me what the radiator says if you find out.

root.line: Hey. I'm Ellis. I took the top bunk. We can negotiate.

choices.label: Keep the top
choices.say: Keep the top bunk. What time is the first bell?

choices.label: Where is assembly
choices.say: Do you know where morning assembly actually is?

choices.label: Did you sleep
choices.say: Did you sleep at all?

bell.line: Eight, I think. Jordan says the first one is only a warning. I didn't ask a warning of what.

choices.label: A warning of what
choices.say: A warning of what?

choices.label: We'll find out
choices.say: Then we'll find out together.

bell-what.line: That's exactly what I should have said. I got as far as nodding.

bell-together.line: Okay. Good. That helps more than I'm going to admit.

assembly.line: Chapel, maybe? Or the hall under the clock. I followed a boy with a cello for a while and then lost him.

choices.label: I'll ask Crowe
choices.say: The groundskeeper is out on the quad. I'll ask him.

choices.label: Which way, the cello
choices.say: Which way did the cello go?

assembly-crowe.line: Tell me what he says. I'm not brave enough to be given directions by him.

assembly-cello.line: Toward the chapel, I think. The case seemed to be the only thing that knew where it was going.

sleep.line: Not really. The radiator talks. Around three it said something and I answered.

choices.label: What did it say
choices.say: What did it say?

choices.label: The top bunk
choices.say: Is the top bunk better for not sleeping?

sleep-said.line: Nothing I can repeat. It was mostly knocking with opinions.

sleep-top.line: You can see the ceiling properly. There's a crack shaped like a river. I've named it. I won't tell you what.

exit.label: Back to the grounds
exit.say: I'll come back for the rest.
exit.line: Go. Keys are in your pocket, I trust. Check.

root.line: North House. I'm Jordan. You want the key, or the bad news first?

choices.label: The key
choices.say: I don't have a room key yet.

choices.label: Lights-out
choices.say: What time is lights-out, really?

choices.label: My trunk
choices.say: Do you know where my trunk is?

key.line: Second floor, room four. I need a signature, and I need you to promise not to copy it. Everyone promises. Some of them mean it.

choices.label: I promise
choices.say: I promise.

choices.label: Why would anyone
choices.say: Why would anyone copy a key to a dorm room?

key-promise.line: Good. That's one more than I had yesterday.

key-why.line: Because the old ones go missing. The house keeps a list. The list is longer than the house.

lights.line: Eleven. The radiator lies and says ten. Past eleven I knock once. After that I knock like it matters.

choices.label: Still reading
choices.say: What if I'm still up reading?

choices.label: The radiator
choices.say: What does the radiator say, exactly?

lights-read.line: Then read quietly. I've never written anyone up for a book.

lights-rad.line: It ticks. It isn't a message. Don't let Ellis tell you it's a message.

trunk.line: On the steps, last I looked. Two trunks, actually. The other hasn't moved since the cab left.

choices.label: The other trunk
choices.say: Whose is the other trunk?

choices.label: I'll fetch mine
choices.say: I'll fetch mine now.

trunk-other.line: Willa Crane's. She's on the steps beside it. Go and say hello when you're ready. She won't mind waiting.

trunk-fetch.line: Lift with your knees. The third step is loose. It's been loose longer than I've been RA.

exit.label: Back to the grounds
exit.say: I'll leave you with the beeches.
exit.line: Thank you. I'll follow when the steps stop being a threshold.

root.line: We came up in the same cab. Neither of us spoke. I took it for good manners.

choices.label: The cab
choices.say: We shared the cab. Did you notice anything on the way up?

choices.label: Your trunk
choices.say: Is that your trunk on the steps?

choices.label: Why still outside
choices.say: Why are you still out here?

cab.line: The driver counted the gateposts under his breath. Eleven. I counted them too, so he wouldn't be alone.

choices.label: I lost count
choices.say: I lost count at six.

choices.label: Why count
choices.say: Why did you count them?

cab-count.line: That's allowed. The last five were the ones that mattered, and they'll be there tomorrow.

cab-why.line: It's what I do when a place is larger than I'd prepared for. I make it a number first.

trunk.line: Mine. The strap gave at the third step, and I put it down to see whether it would mind. It didn't.

choices.label: Let me carry it
choices.say: Let me help you carry it in.

choices.label: Leave it a while
choices.say: Leave it a while. Nobody's going to take it.

trunk-carry.line: Yes. Take the end with the handle. The other end has most of my books, and I'd like them to arrive first.

choices.label: What books
choices.say: What did you bring?

choices.label: I have the handle
choices.say: I have the handle. Lead the way.

trunk-books.line: Seven novels and a dictionary. I'll be sorry about the dictionary on the stairs.

trunk-handle.line: Mind the third step. It's loose. I found out on the way up.

trunk-leave.line: No. It isn't that sort of morning. Everything here seems to be waiting for someone to speak first.

outside.line: Because once I go in, I'm someone who lives here. Out here I'm still arriving, and arriving is easier.

choices.label: Go in together
choices.say: We could go in together.

choices.label: I know the feeling
choices.say: I know that feeling.

outside-together.line: Yes. Together is less like a decision. Let me do the strap first.

outside-know.line: Then stay a minute. We needn't say anything. The beeches do most of the talking here.
